title: Annotatio IV §.III from Posterior (2): Obstinate adiaphora — even into sin and open disobedience
pass_a_gloss: (2.) To cling obstinately to Ecclesiastical Adiaphora because of ingrained custom, even where there is danger of sinning, and likewise with most open disobedience against the Superior Magistrate, through a Zeal owed to ignorance.
pass_b_english: (2.) Cling stubbornly to church adiaphora from long habit, even where sin is a real risk,
and even with open disobedience to the higher magistrate, under a zeal that is really owed to ignorance.
source_text: (2.) Adiaphoris Ecclesiasticis, ob inolitam consuetudinem, pertinaciter, etiam ubi periculum peccandi est, itemque cum apertissima adversus Magistratum Superiorem inobedientia, per Zelum, ignorantiae debitum, inhaerere.
